Class OrderService

java.lang.Object
app.order.OrderService
@Service public class OrderService extends Object
Orchestrates one order submission in two transactions (BR-06).

The first, accept(OrderRequest, UUID), does the idempotency and ownership checks, persists the order as PENDING, runs the trading-rule pipeline, and commits the order as REJECTED or ACCEPTED. An accepted order is the firm's record of intent; once committed, nothing downstream can erase it.

The second is OrderExecutionService.execute(Order, Instrument), which runs in its own transaction and moves the order to FILLED, or REJECTED under the row lock. If execution throws unexpectedly, the failure is written to the audit trail in a short third transaction and the order is returned, and remains, ACCEPTED.

Each transaction raises an OrderStatusEvent for the status it committed, published to Kafka after that commit by TradeEventPublisher. A resubmission that returns an existing order raises nothing.

  • Method Details

    • submitOrder

      public Order submitOrder(OrderRequest request, UUID callerId)
      Submits an order on an account the caller owns. The order is created PENDING; it returns as REJECTED when a trading rule fails, FILLED once the fill is written and the owning user's available funds and the account's holdings have moved, or ACCEPTED when it passed the rules but execution failed unexpectedly, in which case the order stays on record and the failure is in its audit trail. Never throws for a trade that fails a trading rule or whose execution fails; those are outcomes, reflected in the returned order's status, not HTTP-level errors. It throws only when the request names something that doesn't exist or isn't the caller's.

      Ownership is settled before anything else, including the idempotency lookup: an idempotency key is scoped to an account, so answering one before checking the account would hand a caller the outcome of an order on an account they don't own.

      Parameters:
      request - the validated submission
      callerId - the caller's user id, from the token's sub claim
      Returns:
      the persisted order in its current status
      Throws:
      AccountNotFoundException - if accountId does not exist
      ForbiddenException - if accountId belongs to another user
      InstrumentNotFoundException - if instrumentId does not exist
      org.springframework.dao.DataAccessException - if the acceptance transaction itself fails to persist; nothing is then on record
      IllegalStateException - if the account has no owning user

    • getOwnOrders

      @Transactional(readOnly=true) public List<Order> getOwnOrders(UUID userId)
      Lists the caller's own orders, newest submission first. Callers pass the id from the verified token, never an id supplied in the request, so a client can only read orders placed on accounts it owns. A user with no orders gets an empty list rather than an error.
      Parameters:
      userId - the caller's user id from the token's sub claim
      Returns:
      the caller's orders across all of their accounts, newest first
